implementation_statement: The 2022 purchased PCI policy template was never updated for PCI DSS v4.0.1. POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) was approved 2026-08-31 and takes effect 2026-09-01. A one-page onboarding and offboarding checklist covering employees and outside agents is due 2026-09-30.

provider_if_inherited: Processor partner (gateway); CRM vendor; phone vendor; MSP
implementation_statement: The Operations Manager creates console, CRM, and phone accounts on request; the MSP creates suite accounts. Gap: no written approval, no access reviews, and offboarding depends on memory. A former outside agent's console and CRM accounts stayed active for 5 months until 2026-07-15. The phone system has one shared administrator login.
evidence: Console user export; CRM user list; phone admin list; agent roster

implementation_statement: The gateway enforces console roles (administrator, support, sales). Sales agents see merchant status only. CRM folders are restricted so agents see only their own merchants.
evidence: Console role list; CRM sharing settings

implementation_statement: Staff have no local administrator rights on laptops (MSP policy). Gap: all four non-owner staff accounts in the console carry the support role, which can log in as any merchant, although only the two support staff do keyed entry.
evidence: MSP endpoint policy; console role list

provider_if_inherited: Processor partner (gateway); CRM vendor; suite vendor
implementation_statement: The console, CRM, and suite lock accounts after repeated failed sign-ins using vendor defaults (settings confirmed 2026-07-16).

The MSP enforces a 15-minute screen lock on laptops. Gap: PCI DSS 8.2.8 calls for re-authentication after 15 minutes idle, which is met, but the two support laptops used for keyed entry are often left unlocked at home.

Staff reach SaaS systems over the internet; there is no VPN. The MSP reaches laptops through its remote management tool. Gap: no evidence that the MSP tool requires MFA or which technicians have access (requested in P07).
Staff Wi-Fi uses WPA2 with a shared password unchanged since 2023; guest Wi-Fi is separate with internet access only. Support laptops used for keyed entry join the staff Wi-Fi.

Employees watch an annual PCI awareness video. Gap: no phishing exercises, no training on callers who pose as merchants, and no training for the 6 outside agents. Planned: annual training with quarterly phishing simulations and a call-back drill from 2026-10.

provider_if_inherited: Processor partner (gateway); CRM vendor; suite vendor; phone vendor
implementation_statement: The console logs user sign-ins, merchant impersonation, refunds, and settings changes; the CRM and suite log sign-ins and file access. Gap: no list of events the company relies on, and laptop and firewall logs are kept only by the MSP.
evidence: Console audit log sample; suite audit settings

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: nobody reviews logs; the console audit log had never been opened before P07. Planned: a weekly 20-minute review of console impersonation, refund, and settings-change events and suite sign-in alerts, starting 2026-10, recorded on a checklist. A daily alert digest from the console is being set up with the processor partner.
The processor partner keeps console logs for 13 months (gateway documentation). Gap: suite logs are kept only for the plan's default period, shorter than 12 months.

The annual SAQ D for Service Providers is completed by the Operations Manager with the MSP and signed by the Owner. Gap: the 2025 SAQ left out the keyed-entry path. First independent control assessment: P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-05.
evidence: 2025 SAQ D and AOC; P07 results

baseline: High (added by tailoring for PCI DSS)
implementation_statement: Gap: no penetration test has ever been done. PCI DSS 11.4 applies to the company's scope. Planned: an external and internal test of the office network, support laptops, and console configuration by an outside tester by 2027-01-31, then yearly.
The MSP applies a standard laptop image and firewall template. Gap: no written configuration standard, so there is nothing to check the support laptops against.

Gap: console settings changes (hosted payment page content, fraud filter thresholds) are made on request with no approval or record. P07 found unapproved analytics scripts on 2 merchants' payment pages. Planned: a change log with Operations Manager approval for any payment page or filter change, from 2026-09-15.

The MSP keeps a laptop list; the Technician keeps a spare terminal spreadsheet. Gap: no single inventory of systems, data stores, and terminals; the terminal spreadsheet has not been reconciled since 2025.
Gap: no contingency plan. Planned: a two-page plan from the BIA (P05) covering home working, phone forwarding, and vendor contacts, by 2026-11-30.

The MSP backs up the suite daily with 1 year of retention; the CRM vendor backs up the CRM (SOC 2 report). Gap: the suite backup has never been restore-tested and the website bucket has no backup the company controls.
evidence: Backup job report (July 2026); CRM SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: Every employee has a named account in the console, CRM, and suite. Gap: the phone system administrator login is shared by the Operations Manager and both support staff.

provider_if_inherited: Processor partner (gateway); suite vendor; CRM vendor
implementation_statement: MFA is enforced on the suite, CRM, and processor partner portal. Gap: MFA is optional in the gateway console and only 2 of 6 accounts use it; the phone administrator login has no MFA. Planned: MFA required for every console account by 2026-09-15 (processor partner setting).

The console requires 8-character passwords (vendor default). Gap: PCI DSS 8.3.6 needs at least 12 characters, and staff keep passwords in browser storage. Planned: a business password manager and 14-character minimum by 2026-10-31.
Gap: incidents are handled ad hoc. Planned: the P08 runbook for a compromise of the payment environment, with the MSP and the insurer in the chain, approved 2026-08-31; tabletop by 2026-11-30.

Staff tell the Operations Manager about problems informally. Gap: no reporting rule and no recorded contacts at the processor partner and sponsor bank for the 24-hour contract notice. POL-03 4.2 sets a 1-hour internal reporting rule.

Gap: no written incident response plan. The P08 runbook and POL-03 together form the plan required by PCI DSS 12.10.1. 16 CFR 314.4(h) does not apply (314.6 exception), but the plan follows its elements anyway.
Paper with card details or applications goes in a locked shred bin collected by a shredding service. Gap: no record of laptop wiping when two laptops were retired in 2025.
Keyed suite entry with an after-hours alarm; keys held by the Owner and Operations Manager; spare terminals in a locked cabinet. Gap: no visitor log.
This SSP (P02), approved 2026-08-31, describes the Merchant Payments Platform and is the basis for the 2026 SAQ scope description.

Gap: no acceptable use rules before 2026. POL-02 Part C sets workforce and agent use rules, including no card data in email or chat and no merchant data in public AI chatbots; signed acknowledgments due 2026-09-30.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The Operations Manager has acted as security lead since 2023 without a written designation. The Owner designated the Operations Manager as Qualified Individual and PCI DSS lead in writing on 2026-08-31 and took executive responsibility for PCI DSS (POL-02 Part A).
Employees pass a background check before hire. Gap: the 6 outside agents were not screened, although they hold CRM access to merchant owner data.
Employee exits are handled by the Operations Manager. Gap: no checklist and no link to agent contract endings; the former agent's accounts were found active 5 months after the contract ended.
evidence: Agent roster; console and CRM user lists

implementation_statement: First written risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 with NIST SP 800-30 (P01). Not required by 16 CFR 314.4(b)(1) at this size (314.6 exception), but PCI DSS 12.3.1 needs targeted risk analyses that build on it.
An ASV scans the office public IP address quarterly; all four scans in the last year passed. Gap: no internal vulnerability scans of the support laptops or office network (PCI DSS 11.3.1).
evidence: ASV scan reports Q3 2025 to Q2 2026

implementation_statement: The processor partner's AOC is on file. Gap: no list of service providers that touch card data or merchant data, no responsibility matrix, no AOC for the phone vendor, and no security terms in the MSP and web developer contracts.
evidence: ISO agreement; processor partner AOC; MSP contract

implementation_statement: The office firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and separates guest Wi-Fi. Gap: support laptops used for keyed entry share the flat staff network with every other device, so the whole office is in PCI DSS scope.
Console and SaaS sessions use TLS. Gap: merchant applications arrive from agents as unencrypted email attachments, and the phone vendor's call encryption settings have not been confirmed.
evidence: Suite mail flow settings; phone vendor documentation

implementation_statement: Laptops have full-disk encryption (MSP) and the CRM vendor encrypts data at rest. Gap: call recordings held spoken card data and security codes until deleted on 2026-08-14; merchant files sit in the suite and the website bucket without a retention limit.
evidence: MSP encryption report; CRM SOC 2 report; phone vendor deletion letter

implementation_statement: The MSP patches laptop operating systems and browsers monthly and updates firewall firmware. Gap: the website form plugin is two major versions behind, and nobody owns website patching.
evidence: MSP patch report (July 2026); plugin version check

implementation_statement: Antivirus on all laptops, monitored by the MSP in business hours; definitions update automatically.
The firewall's intrusion prevention feature is on with vendor defaults. Gap: no alerting on console events (impersonation, refunds, settings changes) and no monitoring outside business hours.

Gap: no record of what content each hosted payment page carries, so an injected script would go unnoticed. Planned: a payment page script inventory with written justification, removal of unapproved scripts, and a monthly comparison against the inventory until the processor partner confirms its own change-detection covers custom header content.

Gap: no retention schedule. Applications and IDs are kept in email, the suite, the CRM, and the website bucket indefinitely. POL-04 sets a schedule (declined applications deleted within 24 months of the decision).
